claims.claim: **Occurs in heavy users** (daily or almost daily over months) after abrupt cessation or a large reduction. It may not be the presenting complaint — it can arise during any admission.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cannabis withdrawal syndrome' (Last updated December 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cannabis_withdrawal_syndrome/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Time course:** starts 1–2 days after last use, peaks on days 2–6, usually settles in 2–3 weeks; sleep disturbance may persist for months.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cannabis withdrawal syndrome' (Last updated December 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cannabis_withdrawal_syndrome/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Common features:** anxiety, irritability, low mood, insomnia, aggression, headache, nausea, reduced appetite.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cannabis withdrawal syndrome' (Last updated December 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cannabis_withdrawal_syndrome/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Predictors of severe withdrawal:** previous complex withdrawal (aggression, suicidal ideation or attempt, psychosis) · polysubstance dependence · co-occurring mental health or medical conditions (e.g. T1DM, IBD).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cannabis withdrawal syndrome' (Last updated December 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cannabis_withdrawal_syndrome/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Nicotine co-dependence is common** (cannabis is often mixed with tobacco), and **withdrawal from both is more severe.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cannabis withdrawal syndrome' (Last updated December 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cannabis_withdrawal_syndrome/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Distinguish cannabis hyperemesis syndrome** — recurrent severe nausea from regular use, not withdrawal — managed with IV fluids, antiemetics, dopamine antagonists and topical capsaicin cream.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cannabis withdrawal syndrome' (Last updated December 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cannabis_withdrawal_syndrome/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Examine vital signs, look for intoxication or withdrawal, and do a mental state examination.** Severity can be graded with the Cannabis Withdrawal Assessment Scale, which helps grade severity but **is not validated for guiding medication.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cannabis withdrawal syndrome' (Last updated December 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cannabis_withdrawal_syndrome/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Offer opportunistic sexual health, pregnancy and blood-borne virus screening**, and catch-up vaccines (hepatitis B, HPV; consider hepatitis A).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cannabis withdrawal syndrome' (Last updated December 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cannabis_withdrawal_syndrome/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Do not do urine drug screens routinely** — cannabinoids can persist in urine for several weeks.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cannabis withdrawal syndrome' (Last updated December 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cannabis_withdrawal_syndrome/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **For the vast majority, management is non-pharmacological and supportive; no standard medication regimen exists** — only short-term PRN symptom relief.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cannabis withdrawal syndrome' (Last updated December 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cannabis_withdrawal_syndrome/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Psychoeducation** on symptoms, onset, duration and coping; **cravings** — the 3 D's (distract, delay, deep breathing), urge surfing, mindfulness, and check HALTs (hunger, anger, loneliness, tiredness).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cannabis withdrawal syndrome' (Last updated December 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cannabis_withdrawal_syndrome/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Keep the environment quiet, calm, safe and private**; encourage small regular light meals and hydration to avoid dehydration.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cannabis withdrawal syndrome' (Last updated December 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cannabis_withdrawal_syndrome/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Pain/headache:** prn paracetamol 15 mg/kg (max 1 g) four times daily; ibuprofen as needed, 10 mg/kg (max 400 mg) tds; hyoscine butylbromide for abdominal cramps.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cannabis withdrawal syndrome' (Last updated December 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cannabis_withdrawal_syndrome/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **For nausea and vomiting:** oral ondansetron 0.15 mg/kg (max 8 mg) tds prn; cyclizine 8-hourly, 1 mg/kg (max 50 mg), oral, IV or IM; metoclopramide 10 mg tds prn — ⚠️ **risk of extrapyramidal effects with metoclopramide.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cannabis withdrawal syndrome' (Last updated December 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cannabis_withdrawal_syndrome/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Severe agitation or withdrawal:** oral diazepam 5 mg qid prn (**no more than 20 mg per 24 hours**); higher doses only under appropriate supervision; **needs review by a senior clinician; wean over 5–7 days.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cannabis withdrawal syndrome' (Last updated December 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cannabis_withdrawal_syndrome/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Do not prescribe benzodiazepines in the outpatient setting without specialist consultation.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cannabis withdrawal syndrome' (Last updated December 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cannabis_withdrawal_syndrome/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **If severe withdrawal does not respond to diazepam:** oral olanzapine 2.5–5 mg bd prn — **diazepam first; seek specialist advice.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cannabis withdrawal syndrome' (Last updated December 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cannabis_withdrawal_syndrome/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Insomnia:** melatonin 2–5 mg orally nocte.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cannabis withdrawal syndrome' (Last updated December 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cannabis_withdrawal_syndrome/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Concurrent nicotine dependence:** nicotine replacement — **a long-acting patch plus a short-acting form is most effective**; doses per AMH Children's Dosing Companion.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cannabis withdrawal syndrome' (Last updated December 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cannabis_withdrawal_syndrome/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consult the paediatric team** for severe or complex withdrawal (polysubstance use, mental illness, other comorbidities), help choosing the treatment setting or titrating sedatives, or safety concerns.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cannabis withdrawal syndrome' (Last updated December 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cannabis_withdrawal_syndrome/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Transfer if tertiary mental health care is needed.** **Discharge with a clear follow-up plan covering drug and alcohol and psychosocial needs**, and link to post-withdrawal services (associated with better outcomes).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cannabis withdrawal syndrome' (Last updated December 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cannabis_withdrawal_syndrome/, retrieved 2026-09-23
